formula_or_test: SPFM = 1 - [Σ(λ_SPF + λ_RF) / Σλ_SR,HW], equivalently the fraction of the total safety-related hardware failure rate remaining after excluding single-point and residual faults. The compliance test is SPFM ≥ 90% for ASIL B, ≥ 97% for ASIL C, and ≥ 99% for ASIL D.
inputs: λ_SR,HW: total failure rates of safety-related hardware elements
authority: ISO 26262-5:2018, Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 5: Product development at the hardware level ([Kekaoxing][1])
clause_locator: Annex C for the metric calculation; Clause 8.4.5 and Table 4 for quantitative target values
publicly_retrievable: Authoritative ISO publication is paywalled; public copies and national-adoption text are retrievable
volatility: Low; changes only when ISO 26262 is revised

formula_or_test: LFM = 1 - [Σλ_MPF,latent / Σ(λ_SR,HW - λ_SPF - λ_RF)]. The compliance test is LFM ≥ 60% for ASIL B, ≥ 80% for ASIL C, and ≥ 90% for ASIL D.
inputs: λ_SR,HW: total safety-related hardware failure rates
authority: ISO 26262-5:2018, Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 5: Product development at the hardware level ([Kekaoxing][1])
clause_locator: Annex C for the metric calculation; Clause 8.4.6 and Table 5 for quantitative target values
publicly_retrievable: Authoritative ISO publication is paywalled; public copies and national-adoption text are retrievable
volatility: Low; changes only when ISO 26262 is revised

calculation: ISO 26262 probabilistic metric for random hardware failures (PMHF) target
formula_or_test: Evaluate the quantitative hardware-failure analysis for the safety goal and require PMHF < 10^-7 h^-1 for ASIL B, < 10^-7 h^-1 for ASIL C, or < 10^-8 h^-1 for ASIL D. PMHF itself is obtained from the applicable random-hardware-failure analysis rather than a single universal closed-form equation.
authority: ISO 26262-5:2018, Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 5: Product development at the hardware level ([Kekaoxing][1])
publicly_retrievable: Authoritative ISO publication is paywalled; public copies are retrievable
volatility: Low; changes only when ISO 26262 is revised

calculation: JEDEC constant-failure-rate FIT point estimate with Arrhenius acceleration
formula_or_test: For the single-activation-energy case: AF = exp[(E_A/k)(1/T_USE - 1/T_STRESS)]; FIT_POINT = f × 10^9 / (t × ss × AF). Here f is observed failures, t is stress-test hours per device, ss is sample size, E_A is activation energy in eV, k = 8.6×10^-5 eV/K in JESD85A's worked procedure, and temperatures are absolute kelvin.
authority: JEDEC JESD85A:2021, Methods for Calculating Failure Rates in Units of FITs ([Scribd][2])
publicly_retrievable: JEDEC standard is publicly retrievable; third-party copies are also available
volatility: Low to medium; revised periodically as JEDEC reliability methodology evolves

formula_or_test: A_T = exp[(-E_AA/k)(1/T_TEST - 1/T_SYSTEM)] = λ_TEST/λ_SYSTEM. JESD91A specifies k = 8.62×10^-5 eV/K and temperatures in kelvin.
inputs: E_AA: apparent activation energy in eV
failure rates at the two temperatures
authority: JEDEC JESD91A, Method for Developing Acceleration Models for Electronic Component Failure Mechanisms ([Scribd][3])
clause_locator: Clause 2, definition of Arrhenius equation; §5.2 for deriving/using acceleration factors
publicly_retrievable: Authoritative JEDEC text is publicly retrievable
volatility: Low; changes only when JEDEC revises the acceleration-model standard

formula_or_test: For each processing unit, TPP_i = 2 × MacTOPS_i × bit_length_i; aggregate TPP = ΣTPP_i across all processing units on the IC. MacTOPS is the theoretical peak tera-operations/s for multiply-accumulate computation. For classification, compare the resulting TPP and performance density against the 3A090.a/b thresholds.
inputs: largest input bit length for the MAC operation
authority: Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR Part 774, Supplement No. 1, ECCN 3A090, Technical Note 2 to 3A090.a and 3A090.b ([GovInfo][4])
clause_locator: 15 CFR Part 774, Supplement No. 1, ECCN 3A090, Technical Note 2
publicly_retrievable: Free; U.S. export-control regulations and Federal Register text are public
volatility: High; BIS has amended advanced-computing thresholds repeatedly

formula_or_test: Performance density = TPP / applicable die area. Under current 3A090.a, an IC falls into the specified a-classification when TPP ≥ 4800, or when TPP ≥ 1600 and performance density ≥ 5.92. Under 3A090.b, the specified alternatives include 2400 ≤ TPP < 4800 with 1.6 ≤ density < 5.92, or TPP ≥ 1600 with 3.2 ≤ density < 5.92.
authority: Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR Part 774, Supplement No. 1, ECCN 3A090 ([BIS][5])
clause_locator: 15 CFR Part 774, Supplement No. 1, ECCN 3A090.a and 3A090.b; Technical Note 2
publicly_retrievable: Free; U.S. export-control regulations are public
volatility: High; BIS periodically changes thresholds and classification structure

calculation: EAR License Exception LPP cumulative advanced-compute TPP limit
formula_or_test: For a single ultimate consignee in a calendar year, cumulative TPP = Σ individual TPP of eligible commodities. License Exception LPP is available only if cumulative TPP ≤ 26,900,000; a shipment with aggregate TPP ≥ 3,200,000 triggers the specified BIS notification requirement.
authority: Export Administration Regulations, 15 CFR §740.29, License Exception Low Processing Performance (LPP) ([Legal Information Institute][6])
volatility: High; export-control license-exception limits can be amended by BIS

calculation: CHIPS advanced manufacturing investment tax credit
formula_or_test: Current credit = 35% × qualified investment for the taxable year with respect to an advanced manufacturing facility of an eligible taxpayer. Qualified investment is the basis of qualified property placed in service during the taxable year that is part of the advanced manufacturing facility. The 35% rate applies to property placed in service after December 31, 2025; the original CHIPS Act rate was 25%.
authority: Internal Revenue Code §48D, Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit, as amended by Pub. L. 119-21, §70308
clause_locator: 26 USC §48D(a) and §48D(b)(1); Pub. L. 119-21, §70308(b) effective-date provision
publicly_retrievable: Free; U.S. Code and enacted public laws are public
volatility: Medium to high; statutory tax-credit rates can change through legislation

calculation: CHIPS advanced-manufacturing-credit foreign expansion clawback test
formula_or_test: For an existing semiconductor facility, a material expansion occurs when semiconductor manufacturing capacity increases by more than 5% during the applicable period due to added cleanroom, production line, physical space, or a series of such additions. Any construction of a new semiconductor manufacturing facility also qualifies as a material expansion. A significant renovation is separately defined as an aggregate capacity increase of 10% or more from specified physical additions.
inputs: whether the facility is new or existing
authority: Treasury Regulations, 26 CFR §1.50-2, Recapture of the advanced manufacturing investment credit in the case of certain expansions ([Legal Information Institute][7])
volatility: Medium; regulatory definitions can be amended by Treasury/IRS rulemaking
